newsitem.title: USA: Kimberly-Clark net aided by strong personal care unit.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly-Clark net aided by strong personal care unit.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark Corp., maker of Huggies, Scott and Kleenex products, Tuesday reported higher fourth quarter and full year profits and cited strong performance in its personal care paper businesses.

"Continued strong performance in our personal care businesses and the benefits of our merger with Scott Paper Co. drove the record earnings and overcame the adverse impact of lower selling prices for our U.S. consumer and international tissue products and for newsprint," said Chairman Wayne Sanders.
Dallas-based Kimberly-Clark had a fourth quarter profit of $347.1 million, or $1.23 a share, compared with a loss of $841.7 million, or $3.01 a share a year earlier.
Sales rose to $3.32 billion from $3.29 billion.

Fourth quarter sales in the company's personal care products segment rose 15 percent, driven by volume increases in diapers, training pants, incontinence care, baby wipes and professional health care products in North America. Diapers were strong sellers in Europe.
Tissue-based product sales declined 3 percent overall in the fourth quarter because of lower selling prices, which declined 5 percent, and the loss of revenues from divested businesses.
Sales volumes, however, grew 6 percent worldwide, paced by a 9 percent increase in North America, with shipments of both consumer and commercial products up from 1995's fourth quarter.

Revenues from newsprint, paper and other sources were down 21 percent in the fourth quarter principally because of the divestiture of Schweitzer-Mauduit International and sharply lower prices for newsprint.
The company said during the year it integrated its operations with those of Scott Paper Co., realising savings in excess of its target of $250 million.
For the year, Kimberly-Clark earned $1.4 billion, or $4.98 a share, on sales of $13.15 billion. In 1995, it earned $33 million, or 12 cents a share, on sales of $13.37 billion.
Other company brands include Pull-Ups, Kotex, Depend, Kimwipes and Wypall.
Its stock was down $2.50 at $97.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
